What it is

Memory Timeline is a local-first desktop app for recording, organizing, and rediscovering your personal history. Speak a memory — or paste and type one — and the app transcribes it on-device with Whisper, has an LLM extract a structured event, and lets you review it onto an interactive timeline.

Your data lives in a local SQLite database. Embeddings run locally by default, so nothing leaves your machine except the specific text you choose to send to the providers you configure — and geocoding is off unless you opt in.

This site documents the Windows Native app — the primary, actively developed product, built on .NET 10 and WinUI 3.

The memory pipeline

The heart of the app is a single flow, from voice to timeline. Every hop persists its state, so a failure at any stage is recoverable and visible in the UI rather than silently swallowed.

  1. 1
    🎙

    Record

    Windows MediaCapture writes a 16 kHz mono WAV.

    Pause · resume · cancel

  2. 2
    ⏱

    Queue

    recording_queue holds the item (pending → done).

    Audio and text share one queue

  3. 3
    📝

    Transcribe

    Whisper transcribes on-device, fully offline.

    Transcripts persist across retries

  4. 4
    🤖

    Extract

    An LLM produces a structured event into pending_events.

    Dates with honest precision

  5. 5
    👀

    Review

    Edit, approve, or reject each extracted event.

    People flagged new / known / update

  6. 6
    ✅

    Approve

    Event + tags + people + locations in one transaction.

    Atomic write

  7. 7
    🗓

    Timeline

    The event appears and connections update.

    Auto-refresh via the message bus

Text joins audio in the same queue: paste or type a memory (Ctrl+Shift+V) and it enters as a text source whose content is stored as its transcript, skipping transcription entirely.

What's inside

The feature surface of the Windows Native app, grouped by what you are trying to do. The full list lives in the project overview.

🏠

Home & rediscovery

  • On This Day anniversary cards that only surface memories with a real day anchor
  • Guided recall prompts mined from gaps in the archive — never asked twice
  • An optional daily toast and taskbar JumpList shortcuts (the Windows Timeline integration was removed: no callers, and Windows 11 dropped the Timeline UI)
🗓

Timeline

  • Year / Month / Week / Day zoom with smooth pan and keyboard navigation
  • Duration spans, collapsible swimlanes, and uncertainty bands for vague dates
  • Honest date precision — "Summer 2003", never an invented day
  • Coalesced scroll reloads, so fast panning no longer piles up queries
🎙

Capture → events

  • Recording with pause / resume / cancel via Windows MediaCapture
  • Text & paste capture (Ctrl+Shift+V) through the same queue
  • Local Whisper speech-to-text — offline after a one-time model download
  • Media attachments with EXIF, thumbnails, content-hash dedupe and a lightbox
💬

Ask & narrate

  • Ask your timeline — hybrid keyword + semantic retrieval with citations to real events
  • Honest refusal when the archive has nothing relevant
  • Narrative stories from a range, era, or person, exported as Markdown or HTML
🔍

Discover

  • Faceted search across events, tags, people, locations and eras
  • Connections powered by local ONNX embeddings — no API key required
  • A fully offline map with EXIF GPS backfill and manual pin drops
  • Analytics: category distribution, density, tag cloud, people network
🗂

Organize & manage

  • People hub with aliases, case-insensitive identity and merge tombstones
  • Eras, drafts, and append-only revision history
  • .mtbak backup & restore with preview, confirmation and scheduling
  • JSON / CSV / Markdown export, JSON import with duplicate handling

Architecture

Clean, layered separation across six projects, with a message bus between features. Core, Data and Sync target plain net10.0 so a non-Windows head can run them; only the WinUI head and its tests are Windows-only.

MemoryTimeline
Presentation — WinUI 3 + XAML
Views, ViewModels, Controls, Converters, and platform services (audio, STT, notifications, JumpList, navigation, theme).
MemoryTimeline.Core
Business logic
Services for events, timeline, queue, extraction, RAG, ask/query, narrative, resurfacing, recall prompts, media, backup/revisions, export/import and settings — plus DTOs and timeline math.
MemoryTimeline.Data
Data access
EF Core 10 DbContext over SQLite in WAL mode, entity models, repositories, and the SchemaUpgrader that repairs schema drift at startup.
MemoryTimeline.Tests
Verification
xUnit unit, integration and performance tests.
MemoryTimeline.Sync
Sync client (no UI)
Pairing, push/pull/ack against the self-hosted sync service, artifact download, the background sync worker, outbox publishing and remote-change ingestion for the iOS and macOS companions.
MemoryTimeline.SyncContracts
Wire contracts
Shared DTOs from shared-contracts/dotnet/, referenced into this solution and the service. A separate MemoryTimeline.Portability.Tests project, outside the solution, runs the archive stack on the macOS CI job to prove Core, Data and Sync stay platform-neutral.

Decisions worth knowing

Per-operation DbContext via IDbContextFactory

A desktop app has no request scope, so every repository and service opens a short-lived context per operation. This replaced a single app-lifetime context — the root cause of intermittent "second operation on this context" failures.

SchemaUpgrader instead of raw EnsureCreated

Startup creates the database from the current model and idempotently repairs drift (missing tables and columns) on pre-existing databases. A baseline EF Core migration now exists beside it, but nothing calls Migrate() yet — SchemaUpgrader stays the runtime path until the switch-over.

MVVM with a message bus

Cross-feature updates ("event created" → refresh the timeline) flow through WeakReferenceMessenger rather than tight coupling between view models.

Errors are surfaced, not swallowed

Failures propagate to visible InfoBar / status affordances instead of disappearing into logs.

Tech stack

LayerTechnology
UIWinUI 3 + XAML, x:Bind compiled bindings
MVVMCommunityToolkit.Mvvm — ObservableObject, [RelayCommand], WeakReferenceMessenger
Runtime.NET 10 (net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0 for the WinUI head and its tests; Core, Data and Sync target plain net10.0)
DataSQLite via EF Core 10, WAL mode, IDbContextFactory per-operation contexts
AudioWindows.Media.Capture and Windows.Media.Playback
Speech-to-textWhisper.net (ggml base model, local and offline)
LLMAnthropic Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM), routed per call
EmbeddingsLocal ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim, the default) or OpenAI embeddings
Media metadataMetadataExtractor (EXIF taken-date and GPS) + Windows thumbnails
GeocodingOptional Nominatim — opt-in, off by default

Roadmap

  • End-to-end runtime validation of the pipeline and the F1–F12 wave on a real Windows machine
  • Switch runtime schema management from SchemaUpgrader to the regenerated EF Core baseline migration (the migration exists; nothing calls Migrate() yet)
  • Deferred F1–F12 items — photo-import wizard, map tile basemaps, LLM token streaming, PDF narrative export
  • A Settings UI for the Whisper model and language — both are already live settings (whisper_model, whisper_language, re-read on every transcription); there is no picker for them yet
  • MSIX packaging and Microsoft Store submission

Privacy & security

Local-first
All data is stored on your device in SQLite; media is copied into a local managed folder.
On-device transcription
Whisper runs locally — recorded audio is never uploaded.
Local embeddings by default
Connections and Ask retrieval can run entirely on-device with no API key.
Selective cloud calls
Only the transcript text you process reaches your configured LLM provider — which can itself be local.
Geocoding is opt-in
Off by default; coordinates otherwise come only from photo EXIF or manual pin drops.
Secrets at rest
API keys and sync tokens live in the local settings database DPAPI-protected (CurrentUser scope, via the ISecretProtector port); a backup restored under another Windows account reads them as empty and they must be re-entered.
